implementation_notes: Ruby's Enumerable#reduce (aliased inject) is the fold, and operator+ plus an identity value is the instance: [], '', 0, {} are all real identities already. Enumerable#sum takes an init argument, so sum(0) is the total form and raises on an empty enumerable unless the init is given. String + in a loop is quadratic in Ruby too - push to an array and join, or use String.new(capacity:). Enumerable#each_with_object is the accumulator form, and it always needs an explicit accumulator object, which makes the identity choice visible.
pitfalls: Enumerable#sum raises on an empty enumerable with no init - the empty case is where a missing identity shows up.
String#+ in a loop is quadratic; use join or String.new(capacity:).
Array#+ copies the receiver each call; for a fold over many arrays, concat into one accumulator instead.
Hash.new(0) as an accumulator is the identity plus a default - two things at once, and confusing the default with the identity is a common source of off-by-one keys.
